assumptions: How a German bank works the pro rata share isn’t read from any bank’s price list: by the days the account was open in the month, from its opening day where it opened that month, would be SLATE’s reading.
items.ownerDecision: Germany’s month’s fee is charged whole on any closing (banking.ts settleFees, closingFeesOf), where BGB § 675h(3) owes it pro rata to the end. (a) Charge the closing month pro rata: every German close charges less, and three tests whose titles the audit cites (tests/scope-money.test.ts’s Berlin Cancel It and Close It, “refused … for its €4.90 month”, and tests/accountlife.test.ts’s quarter-fee test) assert the whole month on an account opened and closed the same day; their titles would have to change, with the audit pipeline’s inputs, which these instructions forbid an area agent to do. (b) Keep the whole month as SLATE’s simplification and say so in the guide. No played New Haven life closes a German account; a home account at a German bank can be closed (Close It) and would charge less under (a).
